Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The ink flows backward across the corner of the page, reassembling itself into a date.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The numbers are quickly swallowed by the crackle of static on a phone line.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The Old House on the Hill — Living Room.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Maps and missing-person flyers cover the coffee table. A few overdue bills lie buried at the bottom of the pile. Outside, the rain has been falling for three days. The sky has never truly grown light.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man grips his phone, his eyes bloodshot from a night without sleep.

Speaker: Investigator
Dialogue: Sir, we've sent your case file to the search team.

Speaker: Investigator
Dialogue: Most missing-person cases that cross jurisdictions in this state eventually end up with us. We can send people to search the river downstream, the logging camps, and every temporary shelter in the area. Every lead will be independently checked. You don't need to worry about any of that.

Speaker: Investigator
Dialogue: But a search area this large won't be cheap.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I've seen the estimate.

Speaker: Investigator
Dialogue: If paying in full is difficult, one of our partner lenders can arrange financing for up to ten years. A mortgage on your home is also an option.

Speaker: Investigator
Dialogue: Given your current income, however, you could be paying this off for years. Please think it over carefully.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I don't need to think about it. Send me the contract. Take the first payment from my account and finance the rest. List everything I can put up as collateral.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Nothing matters more than my daughter. She's everything to me!

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Send everyone you can. I don't care how far they have to go or what warnings are in effect. Just don't let a single lead go unchecked.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Start now.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: After the call ends, the man keeps the darkened phone clutched in his hand.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His wife sits curled beside the dining table, both hands wrapped around a cup that has long since been washed clean. The rabbit printed on its side has been rubbed so often that half of one ear has worn away.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: I was the one who insisted she wash it that day. What difference would a few more minutes have made? Why did I have to rush her right then...?

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: If I hadn't said that, would she have stayed?

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: No. It wasn't your fault.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man has given her the same answer many times already.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Every time, his wife nods. A little while later, she looks down at the cup and asks the question all over again.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: He reaches for the cup, meaning to take it from her. She suddenly hugs it tighter to her chest.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: A shrill emergency tone blares from the television.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The red alert remains in effect. River levels continue to rise. Multiple landslides have been reported nearby. All residents are advised to remain indoors.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man picks up his raincoat, a flashlight, and the remaining missing-person flyers from the table.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: You're going back out?

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: The roads by the levee are already closed. Even the search-and-rescue teams are pulling back. Wait until the rain eases up... please.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: A lead came in from the shelter downriver last night. Someone saw a child walking alone. About her age.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: But no one's verified it yet.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: That's why I have to go see for myself.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I can't be late again.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His wife grabs his sleeve. The man lays his palm over her icy hand. After a moment, he gently eases her fingers away, one by one.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: Stay here and wait by the phone. Leave the door unlocked.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: If she comes home before I do, I want her to be able to walk straight in.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man folds the missing-person flyers and slips them inside his raincoat, then pushes open the door.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Wind and rain surge into the house all at once.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: When the door closes again, the red alert continues its crawl across the bottom of the screen, washing the cup in red with every pass, the cup no one will ever use for hot cocoa again.

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: Do it.

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: Use the last of your...

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: It's the only thing you can still do for her.
